Discuss the following questions in class: i. Have you ever heard of biotechnology? What do you think it involves? ii. Can you give some examples of products or services that you use in your daily life that might be influenced by biotechnology? iii. How do you think scientists can use microorganisms to help diagnose disease?
3.3.1 INTRODUCTION

The word biotechnology is derived from two words i.e. biology and technology. Biotechnology is the controlled use of biological agents, such as microorganisms or cellular components, for beneficial use.

Microbes such as bacteria, fungi and viruses are found in nearly every environment and make up much of the biomass on earth. They have long been used by humans for several purposes. The use of microbes in biotechnology is known as microbial biotechnology.

Microbial biotechnology is a dynamic field that provides a wide range of products and services to a diverse number of industries. These include food production, drug development, disease prevention and diagnostics, nutritional supplements, energy and alternative fuels, environmental monitoring and waste management, forensic sciences, and many more.
3.3.2 IMPACT OF BIOTECHNOLOGY IN THE FIELD OF MICROBIOLOGY
The use of microbial biotechnology is described below: 1. In Medicine: The concept of microbial biotechnology is used in human and veterinary medicine by the following ways:
a. Antibiotics: Antibiotics are substances obtained from microorganisms that help in controlling different types of diseases. They are obtained from different types of microorganisms.

b. Vaccines: Vaccines are the substances derived from microorganisms used to immunize against disease. Vaccines are produced by using the concept of fermentation technology and recombinant DNA technology. The use of vaccines such as smallpox, polio, tetanus etc. led to the virtual elimination of these diseases in regions of the world where the vaccines have been deployed.

c. Gene therapy: It is a technique that uses genes for the treatment of genetic disorders or chronic diseases. In this technique, new copies of genes are added or replaced by a defective or missing gene in a patient’s cells by the use of genetic engineering.

d. Molecular diagnosis: The early diagnosis of a disease is important to effectively treat the diseases. Recombinant DNA technology is used for isolation and identification of pathogens for easy, early, correct and quick diagnosis of many infectious diseases like AIDs, Cancer, hepatitis, smallpox, etc.
2. In Industries: Microbial biotechnology is used to produce different types of industrial products as follows:
a. Food production: By using the fermentation process different types of alcoholic, bakery and dairy products are obtained.
b. Tea and tobacco industries: The leaves of tea and tobacco are treated with certain bacteria to remove bitterness of leaves, give flavor, colour and taste.
c. Enzymes production: Certain type of bacteria are used to produced enzymes like proteases, pectinase etc.
d. Biofuel production: Biofuel is produced by the use of microbial biotechnology which may be used instead of fossil fuels and are used as a renewable source of energy.
3. In Agriculture: Micro-organisms are found in the soil and help to improve agricultural productivity in following ways:

a. Biofertilizers: Phosphate and nitrogen are important elements for the growth of plants. These elements are found naturally in the environment; however, plants have limited ability to extract them. Microbes, like Penicillium bilaii dissolve the phosphate in the soil and make available to the root of the plants. The bacteria like, Rhizobium, present in root nodules of leguminous plants convert the atmospheric nitrogen into nitrate which are absorb by the root of the plant. These processes take place naturally. However, Biofertilizers are made from these types of organisms when applied by either coating seeds, or putting directly into the soil.

b. Bio-herbicides: Weeds are the plants that compete with crops for water, nutrients, sunlight and space. It also harbors insect and disease. Some micro-organisms function as bio-herbicides because they possess invasive genes that can attack the defense genes of the weeds, thereby killing it. The advantage of using bioherbicides is that it cannot harm the environment and survive long enough for the next growing season.

c. Improvement of variety: By transferring useful genes from microorganisms, improved varieties of crops are produced, enhancing various desirable traits. Improved varieties include the characters like high yielding, high nutrients content, disease resistance variety, pest resistance etc.
